title: UPS Transfer-to-Battery Frequency
dataSources: Proxmox node/VM metrics (`proxmox:metric`), Docker container stats (`docker:stats`), Synology/TrueNAS (`synology:disk`, `truenas:pool`), Raspberry Pi host metrics, UPS status via NUT (`nut:ups`), uptime probes (`uptime:probe`).
app: Proxmox / Docker / Portainer, Synology/TrueNAS, Raspberry Pi, and UPS (NUT) metrics via the Splunk Universal Forwarder, collectd/telegraf, and HEC.
spl:
index=personal sourcetype=nut:ups
| bin _time span=1w
| stats count(eval(status!="OL")) as battery_events by ups_name _time
| where battery_events>3
| sort - battery_events
description: Counts how often the UPS had to leave normal line power, which helps distinguish a stable utility feed from a quietly flaky one.
value: Frequent battery transfers eat into UPS life and explain weird host behaviour; knowing the pattern helps decide whether the real problem is the power feed, not the server.
implementation: Forward NUT status changes into Splunk; review weekly transfer counts and correlate spikes with storms or local wiring issues.
visualization: Weekly chart of UPS battery-transfer events.
grandmaExplanation: It maps how often your UPS has to jump in because the power coming from the wall is not steady enough.
